title: Bigger and smaller
summary: Compare two cities, two prices or two people with the a-CCaC pattern + مِنْ: أَكْبَرُ مِنْ (bigger than), أَصْغَرُ مِنْ (smaller than), أَغْلَى (more expensive).
intro: Yusuf's mother invites Daniel and Layla to lunch, and around the table everyone compares Amman and Cairo. To make a comparative, put the three root letters of the adjective into the pattern a-CCaC and add مِنْ (than): كَبِير (big) → الْقَاهِرَة أَكْبَرُ مِنْ عَمَّان (Cairo is bigger than Amman). The comparative never changes for masculine or feminine. If an adjective has no such form, use أَكْثَرُ (more) + a noun: أَكْثَرُ ازْدِحَامًا (more crowded).
objectives: Make comparatives from adjectives: كَبِير → أَكْبَرُ, رَخِيص → أَرْخَصُ
Compare two things with … أَكْبَرُ مِنْ …
Use أَكْثَرُ and أَقَلُّ (more and fewer)
Compare Amman and Cairo: size, weather and prices

realLife.title: Mansaf at Yusuf's home
realLife.story: Yusuf's family lives on one of Amman's hills, and his mother has cooked the national dish for her son's friends. Over the big tray the conversation turns into a friendly contest: which city is bigger, colder, cheaper or quieter, and which food is tastier.

mistakes.why: To compare, change kabīr to akbar: akbaru min. kabīra min does not mean 'bigger than'.

sentences.en: The weather here is colder than in Cairo.
sentences.literal: the weather here (is) colder than Cairo

sentences.ar: سُكَّانُ عَمَّان أَقَلُّ مِنْ سُكَّانِ الْقَاهِرَة.
sentences.en: Amman has fewer inhabitants than Cairo.
sentences.literal: (the) inhabitants (of) Amman (are) fewer than (the) inhabitants (of) Cairo

sentences.en: Life in Amman is more expensive.
sentences.literal: the life in Amman (is) more expensive

mistakes.why: rakhīṣ has its own comparative, arkhaṣ. Use akthar only with a noun, for adjectives that have no a-CCaC form.

sentences.en: Cairo is more crowded than Amman.

dialogue.title: Amman or Cairo?
dialogue.culture: الْمَنْسَف is Jordan's national dish: lamb cooked in a sauce of dried yoghurt, served on rice and thin bread on one big tray that everyone shares. When food is served, people say صِحَّة وَعَافِيَة ('health and wellness'), much like 'enjoy your meal'. Young guests call an older woman يَا خَالَة ('auntie').

lines.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا أَوْلَادِي! تَفَضَّلُوا، الْغَدَاء جَاهِز. الْيَوْمَ طَبَخْتُ لَكُمْ مَنْسَفًا، وَهُوَ أَكْلَة أُرْدُنِيَّة مَشْهُورَة.
lines.en: Welcome, my dears! Come in, lunch is ready. Today I've cooked mansaf for you; it's a famous Jordanian dish.
segs: mansaf (lamb with yoghurt sauce and rice)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة، رَائِحَتُهُ طَيِّبَة جِدًّا! بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل، وَالْمَنْظَر مِنْ شُرْفَتِكُمْ أَجْمَلُ مِنْ مَنْظَرِ فُنْدُقِنَا.
lines.en: Thank you, auntie, it smells wonderful! Your home is lovely, and the view from your balcony is more beautiful than the view from our hotel.

lines.ar: عَمَّان مَدِينَة جِبَال، وَبَيْتُنَا عَلَى جَبَل عَالٍ. لِذٰلِكَ الْجَوّ هُنَا أَبْرَدُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة، خُصُوصًا فِي الْمَسَاء.
lines.en: Amman is a city of hills, and our house is on a high hill. That's why the weather here is colder than in Cairo, especially in the evening.

lines.ar: صَحِيح! أَمْسِ لَبِسْتُ قَمِيصًا خَفِيفًا وَشَعَرْتُ بِالْبَرْد. وَالْقَاهِرَة أَكْبَرُ مِنْ عَمَّان أَيْضًا، أَلَيْسَ كَذٰلِكَ؟
lines.en: That's true! Yesterday I wore a light shirt and felt cold. And Cairo is bigger than Amman too, isn't it?

lines.ar: طَبْعًا، الْقَاهِرَة أَكْبَرُ بِكَثِير: فِيهَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْ عِشْرِينَ مِلْيُونَ شَخْص. سُكَّانُ عَمَّان أَقَلُّ، حَوَالَيْ أَرْبَعَةِ مَلَايِين.
lines.en: Of course, Cairo is much bigger: more than twenty million people live there. Amman has fewer inhabitants, about four million.

lines.ar: وَالْقَاهِرَة أَكْثَرُ ازْدِحَامًا أَيْضًا! زُرْتُهَا مَرَّتَيْنِ، وَكَانَتِ السَّيَّارَات فِي كُلِّ مَكَان، فِي اللَّيْل وَالنَّهَار.
lines.en: And Cairo is more crowded too! I've visited it twice, and there were cars everywhere, night and day.

lines.ar: لٰكِنَّ الْأَسْعَار فِي الْقَاهِرَة أَرْخَصُ. الْيَوْمَ دَفَعْتُ دِينَارًا لِشَطِيرَةِ فَلَافِل، وَفِي الْقَاهِرَة هِيَ بِعَشَرَةِ جُنَيْهَات فَقَطْ.
lines.en: But prices in Cairo are cheaper. Today I paid a dinar for a falafel sandwich, and in Cairo it's only ten pounds.

lines.ar: صَحِيح، الْحَيَاة فِي عَمَّان أَغْلَى. لٰكِنَّ الدِّينَار الْأُرْدُنِّيّ أَقْوَى مِنَ الْجُنَيْه الْمِصْرِيّ بِكَثِير!
lines.en: True, life in Amman is more expensive. But the Jordanian dinar is much stronger than the Egyptian pound!

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، كُلْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذٰلِكَ! أَنْتَ أَنْحَفُ مِنْ يُوسُف، وَعِنْدَنَا أَكْل كَثِير.
lines.en: Daniel, eat more than that! You're thinner than Yusuf, and we have plenty of food.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا خَالَة، الْمَنْسَف لَذِيذ جِدًّا! هُوَ أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْكُشَرِي… لٰكِنْ لَا تَقُولُوا ذٰلِكَ لِسَامِي!
lines.en: Thank you, auntie, the mansaf is delicious! It's tastier than koshari… but don't tell Sami that!

lines.ar: سِرُّكَ مَعِي يَا صَدِيقِي! لٰكِنَّ سَامِي يُحِبُّ الْكُشَرِي أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَيِّ أَكْل آخَر.
lines.en: Your secret is safe with me, my friend! But Sami loves koshari more than any other food.

lines.ar: وَأَنَا أُحِبُّ الْأَكْل اللُّبْنَانِيّ أَكْثَر! لٰكِنْ يَجِبُ أَنْ أَقُولَ: هٰذَا الْمَنْسَف أَطْيَبُ مِنْ كُلِّ أَكْل أَكَلْتُهُ هٰذَا الشَّهْر.
lines.en: And I prefer Lebanese food! But I have to say: this mansaf is tastier than anything I've eaten this month.

lines.ar: صِحَّة وَعَافِيَة يَا بِنْتِي! وَبَعْدَ الْغَدَاء نَشْرَبُ الشَّاي عَلَى الشُّرْفَة، فَالْجَوّ هُنَاكَ أَلْطَفُ.
lines.en: Enjoy it, my dear! And after lunch we'll drink tea on the balcony, because the air is more pleasant out there.

lines.ar: فِكْرَة رَائِعَة. عَمَّان أَصْغَرُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة وَأَهْدَأُ مِنْهَا، وَأَنَا أُحِبُّهَا كَثِيرًا.
lines.en: A wonderful idea. Amman is smaller and quieter than Cairo, and I like it very much.
segs: I love it (f), I like it

reading.title: Two capitals
reading.ar: أَكَلَ دَانْيَال وَلَيْلَى الْغَدَاء فِي بَيْتِ يُوسُف. بَيْتُ يُوسُف عَلَى جَبَل، وَالْجَوّ هُنَاكَ أَبْرَدُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة. عَمَّان أَصْغَرُ مِنَ الْقَاهِرَة وَأَهْدَأُ مِنْهَا، لٰكِنَّ الْحَيَاة فِيهَا أَغْلَى. دَانْيَال يَقُولُ: الْمَنْسَف أَطْيَبُ مِنَ الْكُشَرِي!
reading.en: Daniel and Layla had lunch at Yusuf's house. Yusuf's house is on a hill, and the weather there is colder than in Cairo. Amman is smaller and quieter than Cairo, but life there is more expensive. Daniel says: mansaf is tastier than koshari!

quiz.prompt: Why is it colder at Yusuf's house?
options: the house is on a high hill

quiz.prompt: Every comparative (أَكْبَرُ, أَصْغَرُ, أَغْلَى) begins with the same sound. Which one?
options: a hamza (glottal stop) with a: ʾa-

completion: Well done! You can compare cities, prices and people with أَكْبَرُ مِنْ and its friends, and use أَكْثَرُ and أَقَلُّ. Next time: the biggest and the best.
